newsitem.title: USA: CollaGenex says Periostat trials successful.
newsitem.headline: CollaGenex says Periostat trials successful.

text.p: CollaGenex Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Friday it presented to dentists evidence that its new drug, Periostat, is helpful in treating adult periodontitis.

CollaGenex said if granted approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, this therapy would be the first orally administered, systemically delivered drug indicated for the treatment of periodontal disease, a leading cause of tooth loss. It said clinical trial results show the investigational drug can, in conjunction with professional oral care, reduce and reverse the progression of adult periodontitis.
"We're very pleased with the results achieved in these extensive clinical studies," said Brian M. Gallagher, president and chief executive officer of CollaGenex.

"Periodontitis is a progressively deteriorating disease for which millions of Americans seek treatment each year. We believe that our drug -- Periostat -- will, if approved by the U.S. FDA, provide an effective new tool to facilitate the dental professional's efforts to fight periodontal disease."
A New Drug Application was filed by CollaGenex with the FDA in August 1996.
CollaGenex is an emerging pharmaceutical company which is developing and commercializing therapies for the treatment of periodontal disease and other dental pathologies.
